### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-defaults/marketplace.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via PackageSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx`  _(via os plugin publish (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/plugin/publish.ts))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-defaults/marketplace.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **143** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e07566b737f80115aa962ae78eac3aa5f103babb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e3e3b33ccfc1b76a09aea94d748ca5e692af6eb0` — the merge of head `5fbe80ef0734936b44eb3f82640601fb59e350b4` into base `e07566b737f80115aa962ae78eac3aa5f103babb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e3e3b33ccfc1b76a09aea94d748ca5e692af6eb0 && git checkout e3e3b33ccfc1b76a09aea94d748ca5e692af6eb0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e07566b737f80115aa962ae78eac3aa5f103babb 5fbe80ef0734936b44eb3f82640601fb59e350b4 && git checkout -B drift-repro e07566b737f80115aa962ae78eac3aa5f103babb && git merge --no-ff 5fbe80ef0734936b44eb3f82640601fb59e350b4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e07566b737f80115aa962ae78eac3aa5f103babb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e07566b737f80115aa962ae78eac3aa5f103babb` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5fbe80ef0734936b44eb3f82640601fb59e350b4`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #20892 (body; comments 5914751356 cloud-seat family note, 5914828402 triage, 5915701788 standing claim, 5916789843 and 5926063883 os-dev-reports, 5917016555 ACCEPT and 5917307077 landing of #20915, 5921173654 director pointer, 5924031583 triage release, 5924884731 round claim and 5926089260 its amendment); the ruling 5921191703 on #20900 (A, its execution parameters, the fork clause); the precedent PR #20915 (body, landed `def279a39b`, an ancestor of this PR's base) and its record 5916999769; PR #21099 body and file list (9 files, +409/−7, head repo objectstack-ai/objectstack, draft, no auto-merge, `Part of #20892`, `Clause-②: yes` first after the colon on line 2); the net diff `git diff 5dbeb7d7b7..5fbe80ef07`; and the check-runs on the head, polled until every latest-per-name run completed. Nothing was built, run or re-run; no worktree, no checkout. The one git operation beyond `show`/`log`/`diff`/`grep` was a `merge-tree --write-tree` probe from a throwaway bare clone sharing the object store (an object read, not a build or a test).

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) `PackageSchema.visibility` `.default('org')` — right, and complete.** `packages/spec/src/marketplace/package.zod.ts:233` moves `PackageVisibilitySchema.default('private')` to `.default('org')`, with a doc comment (L220-232) naming the ruled default and the two CLI commands that now omit the key; the enum and `PackageVisibilitySchema` itself (its describe at L36-40) are untouched. `CreatePackageRequestSchema.visibility` at L308 is still `PackageVisibilitySchema.optional()` with no default — the diff does not touch that line, and the new pin asserts an omitted key stays absent after `parse` (zod sets no key it did not receive), so a create request that omits the key reaches the control plane without it, exactly as the ruling requires. The `DEFAULT_CHANGES_BY_MAJOR[17]` row (`packages/spec/scripts/lib/default-changes.ts:577-596`) is compelled, not optional: `AUTHORABLE_DEFAULTS_DESCRIPTION` in `scripts/lib/authorable-defaults.ts:85-96` states that changing the default of a key that already existed "fails check:authorable-surface until it is declared in DEFAULT_CHANGES_BY_MAJOR", and `build-schemas.ts:3317-3340` prints the copy-pasteable block the dev filled in. The row is correctly shaped: key `marketplace/Package:visibility` matches the ledger self-test's `defKey:name` regex; `from`/`to` are the JSON fingerprints `"private"`/`"org"` in the same quoting as the sibling `ui/RecordChatterProps:position` `"sidebar"` row; it is appended under the current major (spec is `17.5.0`, and only rows at the current major authorise anything, so a wrong major would have gone red); `from` is re-derived against the baseline at the merge base and `to` against what the build emits, so the row cannot outlive the fact. Its `reason` is written for the consumer the ledger header asks for — what moves (a row parsed through `PackageSchema` or its published JSON Schema with no `visibility` reads `org` where it read `private`), what does not (a row or request that writes a value), and the keep-it spelling (`visibility: 'private'`, `--visibility private`) — and it correctly records that `os plugin publish` sent its own `private` explicitly before this change; it carries a ruling date and an ADR id, no tracker number. The two generated artifacts are shown tooling-exact mechanically rather than by trust: `packages/spec/authorable-defaults/marketplace.json` changes one fingerprint line in the shard's sorted set, and `content/docs/references/marketplace/package.mdx:93` changes one default cell to `optional (default: \`"org"\`)`, the same rendering the sibling `publisher` row carries; the lane `Type Check · source gates` runs `check:authorable-surface` (lint.yml:5560) and `check:docs` (lint.yml:5580) unconditionally behind the required `TypeScript Type Check` context, and both are `success` on this head — a hand-edited byte in either file would have made one of them red. The "no `semantic` migration entry" reading is defensible and has precedent on both sides: the ledger header says a default move "that also warrants a migration TODO should get one", the `ui/PaginationConfig:pageSize` move carried `view-pagination-page-size-default-50` because deployed views that omit the key change rendering and `os migrate meta` can materialise it, while the four `enableOnInstall` request-schema rows carried none because nothing in the tree parses those bodies. A package row is a cloud control-plane record: no authored document and no stored `sys_metadata` row carries one (in this repository `PackageSchema` is reached only for `shape.manifestId`, never to parse a row), so there is nothing for `os migrate meta` to rewrite, and the consumer prescription ships in `CHANGELOG.md` through the changeset. The cost, named here so it is not silent: the generated upgrade guide for major 17 will not mention this move; the CHANGELOG will. Acceptable.

**(b) `os plugin publish` — the #20915 shape, line for line.** `packages/cli/src/commands/plugin/publish.ts:71-77`: the flag keeps `options: ['private', 'org', 'marketplace']` and loses `default: 'private'`; its help text says what omitting it does, in the same two sentences as `package/publish.ts:339-340`. L182-186: `pkgBody` is built without the key and `visibility` enters it only under `if (flags.visibility)` — the same statement as `package/publish.ts:536`; the flag's `options` make a falsy-but-present value impossible. There is exactly one `POST .../api/v1/cloud/packages` in the command (L189), shared by create and re-publish, and `--submit` touches only the version body, so the key is absent on create, on re-publish and on `--submit` alike. L197-198: `visibility` is the control plane's answer when `pkg.visibility` is a string, else the value the flag explicitly asked for, else `undefined` — identical to `package/publish.ts:632-633`. L232: `printKV('  Visibility', visibility ?? 'not reported by the control plane')` is identical to `package/publish.ts:755`; `printKV` renders `key: value`, so the line never reads `undefined` (pin 6). L234: the `--submit` hint reads `visibility` instead of `flags.visibility`; its pre-existing guard (`!flags.submit`, `!flags['auto-approve']`) is unchanged, so it now also fires for a `marketplace` plugin re-published without the flag, as the body says. The one difference from `package/publish.ts` is deliberate and right: the package command's hint keys on `ver.listing_status === 'draft'` (L771) because that command prints the listing block; the plugin command keeps its own guard. The plugin `--submit` help text (L81, "Submit for marketplace review after publish") never claimed a `--visibility` precondition, so there is no sentence this change makes false, unlike `cli.mdx`'s `--submit` row in #20915. No `--json` output exists for either command, so the only visible change is a new human-facing `Visibility` line where none was printed before.

**(c) Pins — each would red without its fix; read, not run.** `packages/spec/src/marketplace/package-visibility-default.test.ts` (9 cases): an omitted `visibility` parses to `org` (red under `.default('private')`); each of the three explicit values is kept; `public` is still refused at path `['visibility']`; `CreatePackageRequestSchema` leaves an omitted key absent and carries each explicit value. It imports `./package.zod` the way the four sibling tests in that directory do, and lives under `src/`, which the spec `tsconfig` reaches. `packages/cli/test/plugin-publish-visibility.test.ts` (9 cases: omit, carry x3, re-publish, control, create, not-reported, `--submit`): every pass/fail assertion is about the body the CLI sent or the line it printed; the stand-in `fetch` models exactly the two route facts on the card (patch when the body carries the key; `org` for a new row without it) and `echoVisibility: false` models a non-echoing control plane; the control case (`--visibility private` DOES move a stored `marketplace` row) keeps pin 3 from being vacuous; it stubs global `fetch`, which `postJson` calls (L244); no cross-package read (mkdtemp under tmpdir, imports inside `packages/cli`). The four ablation legs reported by the dev are consistent with the code as read: A reds exactly the omitted-parses-to-`org` case; B (body always carries `flags.visibility ?? 'private'`) reds pins 1, 3, 5, 7 and leaves the three carry cases, the control and the not-reported case green; C (summary reads the flag only) reds pins 3 and 5, because an omitted flag then prints "not reported" where the stand-in answered; D (hint reads the flag) reds pin 3 alone. The dev's "6 red on the unfixed tree" also reconciles: at base the key was always present (pins 1, 3, 5, 7) and no `Visibility` line existed at all (pins 4 and 6), leaving only the three carry cases green. Restores proven by blob equality with HEAD, per the report; the legs were not re-run here.

**(d) Changesets — levels right; every delivered sentence maps to a line of the diff.** `.changeset/20892-package-visibility-default-org.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `Clause-②: yes` first after the colon, no arm; what changes (`parse` of a row without `visibility` returns `org`; the three values read as before; any other value refused), what does not (the accepted values; `CreatePackageRequestSchema.visibility` optional with no default), and the keep-it spelling — each delivered at `package.zod.ts:233` and `:308` and pinned. `.changeset/20892-plugin-publish-visibility-when-asked.md`: `@objectstack/cli: patch`; the defect, the three cases (re-publish keeps, first publish gets the control plane's default — "`org` on ObjectStack Cloud", the same attributed premise #20915 shipped — explicit flag unchanged), the `Visibility` line with its "not reported by the control plane" fallback, and the hint following that answer — each delivered at L71-77, L186, L197-198, L232, L234. Naming follows the issue-number-then-slug precedent; neither body carries a tracker number or a model identifier. One precision flag on the spec changeset is carried to ③.

### ② Semver level

Right: the PR declares `Clause-②: yes` with no arm, `@objectstack/spec` takes `minor`, `@objectstack/cli` takes `patch`. Under `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` a bare `yes` is a widening said quietly and "takes at least `minor`" — satisfied. No `(narrowing)` is owed and none is declared: the accept set of both schemas is byte-for-byte what it was (the same three-value enum, `.default` on the row schema and `.optional()` on the request schema, as before), so no input that was accepted is now refused; the CLI flag accepts the same three values or absence, and the wire drops a key the consumer face declares optional. That is what makes this not BREAKING under the closed set, and why `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`, which judges only changesets that declare breaking, is not engaged and no ADR-0087 disposition is owed — the dev's "no arm, no BREAKING banner, no accepted input refused" reading is the gate's own criterion, not a shortcut. What does move is what the published schema says and what `parse` emits for an omitted key; this repository already treats that class as declared-and-reasoned rather than breaking (the `DEFAULT_CHANGES_BY_MAJOR` row with its printed `reason`; the `pageSize` default move 25 to 50 shipped as `minor` in 17.5.0; the 596090e entry in 17.5.0 declared `yes` "as the conservative arm" when a published declaration's stated meaning moved with no accept-set change). The ruling prescribes exactly this pair (`Clause-②: yes`, minor) and the direction claim is checkable: `check-widening-tells` polices only `no`, and a `yes` can only raise the tier. The CLI `patch` is the #20915 reasoning unchanged — a bug fix in a released package, no accept set moves. The CLI changeset carries no `Clause-②` line of its own; only a breaking changeset must, and the PR's declaration is on the body and the spec changeset.

### ③ Boundary flags

**The fork clause — what this record can and cannot verify.** The ruling's premise is that cloud's `POST /api/v1/cloud/packages` defaults an absent `visibility` to `org`; the ruling itself lists cloud ADR-0007 decision ② as "unverified" and makes the fork clause conditional on the cli seat or the cloud seat reading the route. The dev attempted the read (`add_repo` for objectstack-ai/cloud refused, contents API 403), reported it in the os-dev-report and the PR body, and reported no fork; the seat's amendment 5926089260 states the same. This reviewing session holds no read of cloud either (it is not among the inputs). Verifiable here: the PR's stand-in route encodes exactly the two facts the cloud seat stated in 5914751356 and nothing more; the CLI's behaviour does not depend on the route's default (it sends no key whether the default is `org` or anything else); the ruling closes the question as `org` on protocol grounds, so `PackageSchema.visibility.default('org')` stands on the ruling, not on the route reading; and nothing measured in this repository contradicts the premise. Not verifiable here: the route's actual default for an absent key, and whether its upsert answer echoes `visibility`. What depends on the unverified half is the literal truth of the "`org` on ObjectStack Cloud" sentences (now five user-facing places: the four #20915 landed plus the plugin flag help, with the spec doc comment and the ledger `reason` beside them) and the "declared default and the runtime agree" claim. If a cloud reading ever says otherwise, the ruling's own remedy applies — report the fork on #20892 — and those sentences take a docs follow-up; the obligation is conditional and its condition has not been met, so there is no breach to find.

**Dev deviations — each answered.**
1. `packages/spec/scripts/lib/default-changes.ts` outside the claim's enumerated list — accepted. The gate refuses the ruled default move without the row (①a), the file sits inside the cross-lane package the claim declared, and the seat amended the claim (5926089260) before this record. Named, not silent. Right.
2. A `Visibility` summary line added — accepted. At base the plugin summary printed no visibility at all, so "the summary reads the control plane's answer" (the claim's `:210 and the summary` item) required a line to exist; it mirrors `package/publish.ts:755` byte for byte and is truthful on every branch (①b).
3. No `semantic` migration entry — accepted as a judgment with precedent on both sides (①a), stated in the PR's acceptance note ③ and in the ledger `reason`; not a gate; the CHANGELOG carries the prescription.
4. Branch not merged with `origin/main` — measured here: the head is 28 commits behind `origin/main` `2742e53709` (GitHub's `main` at the time of this read; the dev's `9b81314c29` is its ancestor); no file is touched on both sides; a `git merge-tree --write-tree` from a driverless bare clone exits 0 with tree `abbac60e4ce6`, and the local driver-registered run yields the same tree. Clean; the queue rebuilds the merge.
5. Model-free trailers instead of the harness's model-named one — accepted. Both commits (`2a16679d6b`, `5fbe80ef07`) end with `Claude-Session:` and the model-free `Co-authored-by` pair; the PR body ends with the session-URL footer; no model identifier in title, body, changesets, tests or code.

**Dev out-of-scope notes — each carrier right.**
1. `packages/cli/README.md:111` "There is no `os plugin` command group in v1" — confirmed stale at the head (`plugin/build.ts`, `publish.ts`, `sign.ts` exist). It was false at base, so this change does not make it false and it is not owed in this PR; stale prose is not class a/b/c, so Prime Directive #10 routes it to acceptance notes, not an issue. Today it sits only in the os-dev-report; the seat may append it to the PR body's acceptance notes with a body edit (no new head) or leave it on the card.
2. The `PackageVisibilitySchema` describe (`package.zod.ts:36-40`, "private = owner org only; org = all envs in owner org") — the ruling assigns it to the `domain:spec` seat as a follow-up ("states what `private` actually withholds, measured against cloud's route, or files its retirement under ADR-0049"); it is untouched here and the plugin flag help deliberately does not restate it. Right carrier.

**`Part of #20892`, not `Fixes` — right.** The ruling is four-piece under one card: this code PR and a separate Tier H docs PR closing ADR-0006 v4 open question 2 as `org` with a dated resolution line. That question still reads `private` at `docs/adr/0006-project-environment-split.v4.md:240-242` on this head, so until the docs PR lands the ADR text and the spec disagree — the ruling's own sequencing, not a defect, and the reason the card must stay open. `Part-of PR must not also close its card` and `The card this PR closes must claim this branch` are both green; the claim 5924884731 names this branch.

**Reviewer's own flags.**
- Precision in the spec changeset, not a prescription error: its title calls `org` "the create-time default every publish path already produced", and its body says "no path that creates a package ever reached that value", explaining with the control plane and `os package publish` only. Before this PR `os plugin publish` created packages as `private` by sending the value explicitly, so both clauses are exact only on the reading "every path that relied on a default"; the ledger `reason` and the CLI changeset state the plugin command's prior `private` correctly, and every consumer-facing sentence (what changes, what does not, what to write) is accurate. The compiled CHANGELOG set for the release is therefore not misleading as a whole. The seat may tighten the title before landing (a new head needs a new record) or leave it; this record does not fail on it.
- Scope: the 9 files are the round claim's surface plus the two items its amendment added; no path on any governed surface (`docs/adr/**`, `docs/NORTH-STAR.md`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`); `content/docs/releases/**` untouched; head repo equals base repo, so not a fork proposal; 416 changed lines; draft, no auto-merge.
- Ruling parameters, checked one by one: `.default('org')` ✔; `packages/spec` declared cross-lane in the claim ✔; `Clause-②: yes`, minor ✔; spec artifacts regenerated by tooling ✔ (①a); plugin publish in the #20915 shape ✔ (①b); the four #20915 sentences stay true and untouched ✔ (`cli.mdx:2083`, `publish-and-preview.mdx:168`, the package flag help, its changeset); `CreatePackageRequestSchema.visibility` optional ✔; the governed half kept out of this diff ✔; the describe follow-up left to `domain:spec` ✔; fork clause honoured as far as it could be ✔.

**Gates (check-runs on the head, 35 names, latest per name, converged — every run `completed`):** 33 `success`, 2 `skipped`, 0 failure, 0 cancelled, nothing in progress. The seven required contexts are all `success`: `Lint & Repo Gates` (the last to finish; job 110249393749), `TypeScript Type Check` (aggregator over `Type Check · source gates` / `workspace` / `debt ledger` / `consumer gates`, all success — the lane that proves the two generated artifacts, ①a), `Test Core` (shards 1/6 to 6/6 success), `Dogfood Regression Gate` (shards 1/3 to 3/3 success), `Build Core`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`. Also success: `Check Changeset`, `Part-of PR must not also close its card`, `The card this PR closes must claim this branch`, `No other open PR may claim the same issue`, `No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Build Docs`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Spec property liveness`, `Auto Label`, `Check PR Size`, `filter`.
